To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

IGFBP- 3 protease activity, which is secreted by MDA-MB-231 human breast cancer cells and which results in the disappearance of IGFBP3 and the formation of a 21-kDa fragment that lacks IGF-binding activity, is inhibited in a dose-dependent manner by IGFs under both cell-free and cell-dependent conditions.

IGFBP- 3 is proteolytically degraded by a cysteine/serine protease secreted by MFC-7 human breast carcinoma cells, and that the proteolytic activity of IGFBP -3 is inhibited by IGF-I, but not by IGF-II, under cell-free conditions.
IGF-I and IGF-II, but not IGF analogues, inhibit IGFBP- 3 protease activity in conditioned medium from breast cancer cells, by a mechanism that does not require IGFBP-IGF interaction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of IGF action by IGFBP-4, a member of a family of IGF binding proteins that modulates the availability of the growth factor to the IGF receptors on the cell surface.
the role of IGFs and their binding proteins in the growth regulation of breast cancer cells.
the role of IGF-I and IGF-II in the regulation of breast cancer cell proliferation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the IGFBP- 3 proteolytic enzyme activity secreted by the MCF-7 cell line is not inhibited by IGF-1 or IGF-II in a cell-free system, but that the proteolysis is inhibited when the cells are incubated with the IGFs.
IGFBP-4 proteolytic activity is inhibited by IGFs and IGFBP-2, and this is not mediated by IGF-IGFP interaction.
the IGFBP-1 and IGFBP-2 protease activities in the medium of MCF-7 and MDA-MB-231 breast cancer cells are inhibited by IGFs in a mechanism that does not require IGHF-IGFBP binding.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the IGFBP-5 protease activity is regulated in a complex way.
IGFs regulate IGFBP-4 protease activity, and that IGFs do not require IGFs to bind IGFBP-2 or IGFBP-6 to inhibit IGFBP protease activity.
IGF-I and IGF-II can inhibit IGFBP- 3 proteolysis without requiring IGF binding to IGFBP.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IGF-I and IGF-II are potent inhibitors of IGFBP proteolysis by MCF- 7 cells.

IGFBP- 3 protease activity is inhibited by IGF-I in a manner that does not require IGFBP-IGF-I interactions, suggesting that IGF-I may regulate its own action in breast cancer cells by inhibiting IGFBP- protease activity.
IGFBP proteolysis by the IGFBP-1 protease and IGFBP-2 protease is not inhibited by IGFBPs or IGFs.
